clue.text: Leave one's bed and dress

definitions.note: verb phrase; the grid form is hyphenated

blocks.note: first meaning: to rise in the morning
second meaning: an outfit, especially an unusual or elaborate one

explanation.surface: Someone's morning routine: out of bed and into clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: As a verb (get up) it means to rise; as a noun (a get-up) it is a costume or outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Rising from sleep is the verb phrase, while a get-up is an informal noun for a costume or set of clothes.

clue.text: Obtain approval for use

blocks.note: first meaning: a bill or deal is passed
second meaning: to use up or consume, as in going through money

explanation.surface: Getting permission before something may be employed.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal goes through when it is accepted, and you go through supplies when you consume them completely.

clue.text: One may get a raise after a good performance

definitions.text: One may get a raise after a good performance

blocks.clueFragment: One may get a raise after a good performance
blocks.note: surface reading: an employee who earns a pay rise for doing well
setter's reading: a digit literally lifted in approval when something has gone well

explanation.surface: An employee rewarded with a pay rise after a strong appraisal.
explanation.walkthrough: Raise means a salary increase in the surface, but here it is a physical lifting: the thumbs-up gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising this digit, a thumbs-up, signals approval, which is what follows a good show or job well done.

clue.text: Peanut I cultivated for blossom

indicators.note: cultivated soil is worked over and turned, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener growing groundnuts for their flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: The petunia is a popular bedding plant grown for its trumpet-shaped flowers, an example of a blossom.

clue.text: Staff do head off finally, given direction

indicators.note: finally points at the closing letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: bean is slang for the head
the last letter of off
a compass direction

explanation.surface: An office party where the boss slips away at the end, after giving instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' reads as leaving, but head is BEAN and only the final letter of off is used. A beanfeast is an old British name for an annual works dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A beanfeast was traditionally the yearly celebration an employer laid on for workers, so a staff party or celebration.

clue.text: School upholding British language

indicators.note: in a down entry, holding up means sitting underneath, so the piece named first comes below

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
Eton College, the English public school

explanation.surface: A school that defends the English language.
explanation.walkthrough: Upholding works because this is a down answer: the school sits below and supports British.
explanation.definitionFit: Breton is the Celtic tongue spoken in Brittany, in north-west France, so a language.

clue.text: Soldier, perhaps, I love excessively — here's a remedy

blocks.note: a soldier is one kind of ant
taken as written
to dote is to love to excess

explanation.surface: Someone confessing to an infatuation with a soldier and offering a cure.
explanation.walkthrough: Soldier is not a person here: soldier ants are a caste of ant.
explanation.definitionFit: An antidote counteracts a poison, so it is a remedy, synonym-level and also used figuratively.

clue.text: Man limited by a daft disposition?

definitions.text: Man limited by a daft disposition?

indicators.note: something limited is bounded on each side, so one piece is held within another
a disposition is an arrangement, so these letters are disposed in a new order

blocks.note: he is a male pronoun
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A person held back by a silly temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: someone hemmed in by foolishness is a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Fathead is an informal insult for a stupid person, one whose silly nature defines them.

clue.text: Challenger of decision that's cut wealth in a factory

indicators.note: cut means trimmed short, so the word loses its final letter
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a plant is a factory
pelf is money or wealth, usually dishonestly got

explanation.surface: Someone disputing a ruling about reduced riches in an industrial plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Pelf is an old, usually disparaging word for money; with its tail cut it slots in after the first letter of the factory word.
explanation.definitionFit: An appellant is a party who lodges an appeal against a court ruling, so a challenger of a judgment.

clue.text: Dishonestly lose project

blocks.note: first meaning: to lose a contest deliberately
second meaning: to hurl or propel

explanation.surface: Someone crookedly losing a piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: Project reads as a noun, a scheme, but it is the verb meaning to cast forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw a fight is to lose it on purpose for gain, and to project an object is to hurl it.

clue.text: Brown I found in trial to be most reliable

indicators.note: something found in another lies inside it, so the first pieces sit within the last

blocks.note: rust is a reddish-brown colour
taken as written
a trial is a test

explanation.surface: Someone named Brown proves, under examination, the most dependable of the group.
explanation.definitionFit: Trusty means dependable, so its superlative describes the one who can be relied upon above everyone else.

clue.text: By joining part-time soldiers, one may get used to light fire

definitions.text: one may get used to light fire

blocks.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
per means by, as in 'per post'

explanation.surface: Reservist soldiers learning to cope with being shot at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get used to light fire' sounds like soldiers becoming accustomed to gunfire; really a taper is used to light a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A taper is a slender wax-coated wick or spill, lit from one flame and carried to kindle a fire or candles.

clue.text: Spirit clothin' saint?

blocks.note: robing means clothing; the apostrophe drops its final G, as clothin' drops its G
a saint is a very good fellow, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A ghost wrapped up in a holy man's robes.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped G in clothin' tells you to drop it from robing too. Robin Goodfellow is Puck, the mischievous sprite of English folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Goodfellow is a hobgoblin of English folk tradition, a household sprite or fairy, so a spirit.

clue.text: Cheerful mug? Just the reverse

blocks.note: to mug someone is to beat them up; this is the second word of that phrase
the instruction to put the first word of the phrase second

explanation.surface: A cheerful face, or a cheery remark answered with its opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: Mug means BEAT UP; 'Just the reverse' swaps the two words, not the letters, to make UP BEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Upbeat is an informal adjective for optimistic and positive in mood, matching cheerful as a synonym.

clue.text: Steps taken to get ramshackle car banned

indicators.note: ramshackle means tumbledown and disordered, so these letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Action taken to get a decrepit old car off the road.
explanation.walkthrough: Steps taken sounds like measures adopted; here it is dance steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A barn dance is a lively country dance, a social gathering of folk-dance figures, so a series of steps.

clue.text: Equine establishment where boss removed mare

blocks.note: a boss is a raised stud or knob
far removed means distant
m is the abbreviation for mare in horse-racing form

explanation.surface: A stable yard where the manager has taken a mare away.
explanation.walkthrough: Boss looks like the person in charge but is the ornamental knob; m for mare is the racing-card abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud farm is where horses are kept for breeding, so an establishment devoted to equine stock.

clue.text: Out east, sell vehicle for writer

indicators.note: out means removed, so the compass letter for east is taken away

blocks.note: to market goods is to sell them
a wain is a farm wagon

explanation.surface: Someone in the Far East selling a car to a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Out east looks like a place; it means removing E from MARKET.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain was the pen name of Samuel Clemens, the American novelist behind Huckleberry Finn.

clue.text: Poet follows despicable fellow, one carrying a sword

indicators.note: follows puts the first-named piece after the second

blocks.note: a scab is a contemptible person, especially a strike-breaker
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A poet tailing a scoundrel who is armed with a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: One carrying a sword sounds like a person; it is the sheath that holds the blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A scabbard is the sheath in which a sword's blade is housed, so the thing that holds it.

clue.text: Tough course for sailors?

blocks.note: tough means hard
a tack is the course a sailing ship takes relative to the wind

explanation.surface: A difficult route a ship has to sail.
explanation.walkthrough: Course reads as a nautical heading, but the whole clue also means a tough food course eaten by sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardtack is the hard dry ship's biscuit long issued as rations at sea, a tough dish for mariners.

clue.text: Puzzle — hint given by computer store

blocks.note: a tang is a hint or trace of flavour
random-access memory, where a computer stores data

explanation.surface: A clue to a puzzle supplied by a computer shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Computer store reads as a shop; it is the machine's memory.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangram is a Chinese dissection puzzle of seven flat pieces arranged to form shapes.

clue.text: Carried away by golden eagle, say

blocks.note: rapt means enraptured, carried away
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Something snatched up and carried off by a golden eagle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Golden eagle' looks like one bird, but golden is OR on its own and eagle is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A raptor is a bird of prey, and an eagle is one example of such a hunting bird.

clue.text: Difficult days in a hospital room

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a week, seven days, abbreviated
a ward is a room in a hospital

explanation.surface: A tough stretch of time spent on a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: Days means a run of seven of them, a week, abbreviated WK.
explanation.definitionFit: Awkward means hard to deal with or handle, as a difficult situation or person is.

clue.text: Chap calling for food to be laid in a pub

indicators.note: laid in means set down inside something

blocks.note: a bar is a pub
an egg is a food, and eggs are laid

explanation.surface: A man asking for something to eat to be served in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chap calling for food' looks like the definition, but only Chap is: beggar is informal for a fellow, as in 'lucky beggar'. Laid suits the food, which hens lay.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal British speech a beggar is simply a person or fellow, as in 'you lucky beggar', so a chap.

clue.text: Way of dealing with shares in accommodation

blocks.note: first meaning: selling shares and buying them back next morning, for tax purposes
second meaning: a guesthouse offering a room and morning meal

explanation.surface: A method for handling a share of the lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, bed-and-breakfasting shares meant selling them one evening and rebuying them the next morning to realise a gain or loss for tax.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a stock-market tax manoeuvre and the familiar lodging offering overnight stay plus morning meal.

clue.text: Suit to keep in good shape

blocks.note: first meaning: to be appropriate for
second meaning: split into two words, to be in good physical condition

explanation.surface: A suit designed to stay looking sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second half as two words, be fit.
explanation.definitionFit: To befit is to be suitable for, and being fit means being healthy and in good physical condition.

clue.text: Analysis revealing arsenic, for example

blocks.note: As is arsenic's chemical symbol
say means for example

explanation.surface: A laboratory test finding traces of poison.
explanation.walkthrough: In the surface, arsenic is the example found; in fact for example gives SAY on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: An assay is a test determining the composition or purity of a substance, especially a metal ore.

clue.text: Better putting one new sovereign on filly

indicators.note: putting one thing on another places pieces side by side

blocks.note: f is the abbreviation for filly in racing form
Roman numeral one
standard abbreviation
Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A gambler betting a gold sovereign on a young horse to improve their fortunes.
explanation.walkthrough: Sovereign looks like the gold coin, but it is the monarch, ER. In a down-the-page sense, 'on filly' means these letters follow F.
explanation.definitionFit: Finer is the comparative of fine, meaning of higher quality, which is what better also means.

clue.text: It separates grease from turkey, we hear

definitions.text: It separates grease from turkey, we hear

blocks.note: surface reading: a kitchen gadget that skims the fat off a roast bird
setter's reading: say grease and it is the name of a country, so the clue means a stretch of water dividing two nations

explanation.surface: A cook's gravy separator taking fat off the Christmas bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Grease spoken is Greece and turkey is Turkey; the body of water between the two countries is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This arm of the Mediterranean lies between the Greek mainland and the Anatolian coast, dividing the two countries.

clue.text: The army corps I'd join with other soldiers once a month

indicators.note: joining things together places them one after another

blocks.note: taken as written
the Royal Marines, a corps of soldiers
taken as written without the apostrophe
other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A military unit merging with more troops on a monthly schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: Once a month reads as 'monthly' but means a month that once existed: Thermidor was the eleventh month of the French Revolutionary calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermidor, the summer month of heat in France's revolutionary calendar, is a former month no longer used.

clue.text: College's senior member — about the oldest?

definitions.text: College's senior member — about the oldest?

indicators.note: about means going round, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: a don is a senior fellow of a university college
ye is the oldest written form of the

explanation.surface: Asking whether a college's leading fellow is roughly the eldest there.
explanation.walkthrough: Ye, as in 'Ye Olde Tea Shoppe', is an archaic spelling of the. The whole clue also defines the answer: the most senior member, often the oldest.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyen is the most respected or longest-serving member of a group, typically its senior and eldest figure.
